frontmatter.summary: H2 order flipped: shift swaps ships first, payroll export moves to Q1 2027

input.body:
Åsa reversed the May order at steering on 2026-07-16: shift swaps ([[tickets/jira/SCH-231]]) ships first, payroll export ([[tickets/jira/SCH-118]]) moves to Q1 2027 ([[meetings/{{date:2026-07-16}}-steering]]).

The May reasoning was that two accounts had asked for the export with a date attached and nobody had a hard date on swaps ([[decisions/2026-05-18-h2-order-payroll-first]]). That no longer holds. Café Nord's QBR put a date on swaps that we did not choose: their staff turn over every September and managers rebuild the week by hand because staff cannot swap shifts themselves ([[insights/cafe-nord-september-turnover]]). Two more chain accounts in the pipeline asked the same question in the same week, one of them with over a hundred locations. Payroll export helps none of the three.

Both epics sit on one team, so the second one moves a full quarter, not a few weeks ([[notes/h2-capacity]]). Åsa took that cost on purpose: "that's the whole point of doing this today instead of next month."

Not decided here: a ship date for swaps. Rebecca re-estimates [[tickets/jira/SCH-240]] by 2026-07-24, and that number is an estimate, not a promise.
input.rationale: Åsa decided it in the room with a named reason, and it reverses the May order, so it is a new decision that supersedes the old one.

input.append:
## Summary

Åsa flipped the H2 order: shift swaps ships first, payroll export moves to Q1 2027 ([[decisions/{{date:2026-07-16}}-h2-order-swaps-first]]). The May reasoning was two accounts with a date on the export and nobody with a date on swaps ([[decisions/2026-05-18-h2-order-payroll-first]]). Since then Café Nord's QBR and two more chain accounts in the pipeline asked the same question, unprompted: can staff swap their own shifts. All three hit the September turnover, six weeks out, and payroll export helps none of them.

Rebecca's two conditions. The last swap story, manager approval with the overtime check, is a data problem, not a UI problem: it touches the same schedule-recalc path as payroll export. She re-scopes [[tickets/jira/SCH-240]] and gives a real estimate, not a ship date, by 2026-07-24. And the swap notification shows the requesting colleague's name and phone number, which Henrik has not seen. Åsa: "that's not optional." I ping Henrik today ([[todos/henrik-review-swap-notifications]]).

A fourth story nobody has written: when a swap is approved, the colleague who gave up the shift is not told by the app. Today that is a message the manager sends by hand. Åsa wants it filed under [[tickets/jira/SCH-231]] this week.

For Café Nord the line stays "before September", as Marcus said at the QBR, and nothing firmer until Rebecca's number lands. If Lena pushes: "more in a couple of weeks", not a new date.

## Notes

- Roadmap H2 still says export first, swaps second. Åsa wants it flipped today, and a comment on [[tickets/jira/SCH-118]] saying the export moves to Q1 and why.
- Marcus: "my slides already say September." Rebecca: "then your slides are wrong."
- Rebecca has the Fortnox connector demo on Wednesday, so the estimate is next Friday, not this one.
input.rationale: The write-up of yesterday's steering: the order flip, Rebecca's estimate date, the GDPR gap, the fourth story, and what Café Nord gets told.

input.body:
Payroll export moves from Q3 to Q1 2027. Shift swaps (SCH-231) ships first. Åsa flipped the order at steering on 2026-07-16: three chain accounts hit the same September staff turnover and asked for swaps, and the export helps none of them.

What happens next: Rebecca re-estimates SCH-240 by 2026-07-24, an estimate and not a ship date. The Roadmap H2 page is being flipped to match.

Source: Steering, 2026-07-16
input.rationale: Åsa asked for a comment on the payroll epic saying it moves to Q1 and why, so nobody watching the ticket is surprised in three weeks.

input.title: Notify the affected colleague when a swap is approved
input.body:
Part of SCH-231. When a manager approves a swap, the colleague who gave up the shift hears about it from the app. Today that is a message the manager sends by hand, if they remember, and support will hear about it once swaps are live for real customers.

Not one of the three stories in the epic. Raised by Rebecca at steering on 2026-07-16; Åsa asked for it filed this week.

Acceptance:
- [ ] When the manager approves, the colleague who gave up the shift gets a notification naming the shift and who took it.
- [ ] The colleague who took the shift sees it on their published schedule at the same moment.
- [ ] Nothing is sent while the request is still pending or after a rejection.

Source: Steering, 2026-07-16
input.rationale: Agreed work that nothing in the epic covers. Åsa: "then write it."
